Twelve ingots of the Nb-Al-Mo ternary compositions were melted and cast by the induction skull melting facili- ty at Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding Co.
Specimens were hipped at 2073 K, 0.2 MPa for 14.4 ks.
These specimens were cut to small blocks and annealed at high temperatures (1873 K for 3.6 ks and 2073 K 1.8 ks) in vacuum, then quenched to
the room temperature by introducing He gas into the chamber.

Tensile specimens were heated up to the test temperature and hold for 1.2 ks, then deformed with a constant strain rate of 5 x 10-4 s -1 at various tem- peratures (1773 to 2073 K) in a vacuum (10-3 Pa).
